research_method.claude: Systematic mapping study (Petersen et al.); database search plus backward snowballing and forward-citation check; axial coding and open card sorting; 1,643 raw records, 1,151 unique, 131 after screening plus 29 via snowballing = 160 studies; 146 interventions; Fleiss' kappa 0.79
research_method.nlm: Systematic mapping study following Petersen et al. and Kitchenham et al.; 160 primary studies selected from 1,643 raw records and validated via snowballing; 146 interventions mapped to 5 facets and 8 KPIs
research_method.value: Systematic mapping study (Petersen et al. guidelines, Kitchenham-style screening); 1,643 raw records, snowballing, 160 primary studies included; 146 interventions coded into an Intervention → Dev-X facet → software outcome → business KPI taxonomy (5 facets, 8 KPIs, 5 relationship types)
research_method.note: Screening counts and kappa reported only by Claude (not contradicted).

context.claude: Mixed (primary studies from industry, OSS and academia); secondary review of 160 studies
context.nlm: Industrial, OSS, academic and mixed settings across 160 primary studies
context.value: academic (secondary/review); 160 primary studies (industry, OSS and academic settings)

dora_applied.note: Claude: not cited; NotebookLM: referenced only. 'DORA' does not occur in the full text.

space_applied.note: Claude: not cited; NotebookLM: referenced only. 'SPACE' does not occur in the full text.

ai_discussed.note: AI-assisted/LLM/GenAI interventions mapped (S81, S90, S63, S112) and reported as an emerging 2021-2024 trend.

remote_covid.note: Claude: work mode not reported (one COVID-19 primary study). NotebookLM: not specified, only settings of some primary studies. Full text has one sentence on pandemic-era well-being studies (Section 5.3).

cat_quality.note: Quality KPI is the most frequent (67 instances, 41.9%).

cat_collaboration.note: Team Dynamics KPI (trust, cohesion, coordination; 27 instances).

cat_satisfaction.note: Emotional States facet and Developer Well-being KPI.

cat_activity.note: Borderline: commits appear only as an example indicator of the Productivity KPI, and the commit ratio (DCR) comes from one primary study; activity is not a synthesized category.

cat_delivery.note: Claude: Process Efficiency KPI with lead/cycle time indicators (15 instances). NotebookLM names Process Efficiency without indicators and gives no delivery metric.

cat_devex.note: Claude: facets built on Fagerholm & Münch, Greiler/Storey/Noda only referenced. NotebookLM: Greiler et al./Storey et al. dimensions applied. Cognitive Load (facet) and Flow (KPI) are synthesized; Noda/Storey/Forsgren 2023 not found in text.

cat_agile.note: Claude: Process Efficiency KPI (WIP, adherence to process, lean flow efficiency). NotebookLM: Agile/Scrum/XP only as interventions, no process metric.

cat_survey.note: Perceptual instruments (NASA-TLX, PANAS/affect grids, motivation scales, survey ratings, perceived productivity) used to code facets and KPIs.

evidence.quote: We conducted a systematic mapping study of 160 empirical articles published between 2006 and 2024.
We aggregated results from all databases into a unified corpus, resulting in 1,643 raw records.
We selected October 2006 as the lower bound to capture early empirical studies on developer cognition, affect, and values
evidence.loc: 3.3. Article search and selection (Time Window Justification)

evidence.quote: In parallel, intervention designs increasingly include AI-assisted [S148] [S42] and no/low-code and GenAI-specific constructs [S112] (trust, zero-shot emotion analysis).
evidence.loc: 5.3. Longitudinal shifts in Dev-X intervention design and KPI focus

evidence.quote: The most frequently reported KPI was Quality Outcomes (67), followed by Productivity (55), Team Dynamics and Culture (27), and Project Success (19).
evidence.loc: 4.1. RQ1: Mapping Dev-X facets, relationship types, and business KPIs

evidence.quote: Productivity Effective output per unit time; perceived productivity; throughput/velocity. Indicators: commits, tasks completed, cycle time, survey ratings.
Quality Internal/external quality: defects, smells, readability, review rework, static warnings. Lower defect density; improved readability; less rework.
Team Dynamics Trust, cohesion, coordination, conflict, retention risk, culture. Higher trust/cohesion; fewer conflicts; better coordination.
Developer Well-being Burnout, stress, recovery, psychosocial risk and satisfaction. Lower burnout/stress; improved well-being scores.
Emotional States Valence-Arousal-Dominance and discrete emotions; cues: affect grids/PANAS, sentiment/lexicons, mood induction, physiological proxies.
